references.text: Joshua gives instructions about the ambush that was to lie west of the city, which prepares for the action described in verse 13.
Joshua sent the ambush to lie in hiding between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai, which is the same military strategy.
Describes the location of the main force north of the city and the ambush west of the city, which directly corresponds with verse 13.
The first failed attack on Ai provides context for why Joshua now uses a more cautious military strategy with an ambush.
Gideon uses a similar nighttime military strategy against the Midianites, where he moves in the darkness to surprise the enemy.
The Lord gives Joshua a special military strategy to take Jericho, which sets up the pattern of divine guidance in Joshua's conquests.
